application_targets.label: SATISFIED
application_targets.exact_quote:
The Madras-Bangalore Transport Company, a partnership firm, became the tenant of the disputed premises in July 1962.
This was in 1968.
application_targets.reason: The tenancy began in 1962 and the company whose occupation generated the section 14(1)(b) controversy was formed in 1968, placing the relevant alleged event after 9 June 1952.

application_targets.label: UNRESOLVED
application_targets.reason: The target court recites the landlord's allegation that consent was absent but does not itself make an independent finding on written consent. Because every substantive route was rejected, the consent proposition was unnecessary to the target merits disposition.
application_targets.uncertainty: HIGH: absence of consent remains an allegation rather than an independent target finding.

application_targets.reason: The supplied subletting qualification requires tenancy incidents including a right to possession against the tenant. The target court's retained-occupation finding defeats the possession-transfer component and it expressly finds no subletting; it did not need to decide every other listed incident separately.
application_targets.uncertainty: MEDIUM: the possession prong is expressly defeated, while payment of rent and other incidents were not separately adjudicated.

application_targets.label: DEFEATED
application_targets.exact_quote: the Madras-Bangalore Transport Company (West) continued to be in occupation of the premises even after the Caravan Goods Carrier Private Limited came in. They never effaced themselves.
application_targets.reason: The parting-with-possession qualification requires divestment of legal possession. The target court affirmatively found continued occupation and no effacement, defeating the required divestment.

application_targets.label: SATISFIED
application_targets.exact_quote:
merely because the Caravan Goods Carrier Private Limited was a legal personality distinct from the firm and its partners and it operated from the disputed premises.
From the facts established on the evidence we do not have any doubt that the Caravan Goods Carrier Private Limited was an alter ego or, if we may be permitted to use such an expression, 'the corporate reflection' of the partnership firm of Madras-Bangalore Transport Company (West).
They never effaced themselves.
application_targets.reason: The target court expressly rejected treating separate corporate personality as dispositive, examined the actual relationship and continued possession, and found substantial identity rather than ouster. That is the precise corporate-form qualification supplied by C8.

issue_target.reason: The Supreme Court decided the fixed issue on the merits and held that none of the three statutory routes was established.
issue_target.procedural_limit: The absence of an independent target finding on written consent does not matter to the issue result because the target court expressly defeated all three alternative routes.
